behavior: A patient, diurnal hunter that stands still or walks slowly through shallow water, then strikes fish and other small prey with a rapid thrust of the neck and bill. Flies with the neck retracted and legs trailing. Usually nests colonially in trees or shrubs near water.
field_marks: Entirely white plumage; breeding adults develop long, wispy back plumes
Tall, slender proportions with a very long, S-curved neck
Long, straight, daggerlike bill, usually yellow to orange
Pale yellow eye with yellow-green bare facial skin
Very long, usually dark legs and feet
Broad, rounded white wings and a short tail; legs extend well past the tail in flight
habitat: Freshwater and saltwater wetlands, including marshes, ponds, lake and river margins, estuaries, lagoons, mudflats, wooded swamps, and other shallow-water shorelines; nesting sites are typically trees or shrubs near water.
